chunks: And through his chain of narration, from Ali (peace be upon him), he said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to me:
“Whatever road you take or pass, Satan will take the opposite road and pass the opposite way.”
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet tell Ali about the relationship between his path and Satan's path?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, this hadith highlights the cosmic opposition between the believer and Satan, emphasizing that spiritual progress inherently creates distance from evil. It underscores the Shia concept of *Muqabalah* (counter-position), where the faithful’s adherence to divine guidance naturally repels the devil’s influence, serving as a practical indicator of one’s spiritual state.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-277 According to the same documentation, it is narrated that Ali (a.s.) said that God’s Prophet (S) told him,
“Whatever road you take, Satan will go the opposite way.”
